penetration_assumption: Sized against the RETAIL aisle only (Rs 3,96,245 / 12m), not the Rs 12.76 L category total — 69% of the category is one Delhi wholesale customer and would not buy any of these. Line by line, in plain words: (1) CHILKA — ARY sells 628 urad packs/yr (370 dhuli + 258 sabut) and 1,313 moong packs/yr (927 dhuli + 386 sabut) at retail; chilka is the third form of the same pulse, and I assume it takes 20% of the combined dhuli+sabut volume of its own pulse (126 urad + 263 moong = 389 packs of 500g at ~Rs 60), of which only 60% is incremental because the rest cannibalises dhuli/sabut = Rs 13,997. (2) MANGODI/MOONG BADI — no substitute exists on the shelf, winter-only (Nov-Feb), assume 100 packs of 400g at Rs 90 = Rs 9,000, fully incremental. (3) BHATT + MOTH — priced off the store's own live pahari proof point: Raja Kulath Daal did 109 packs in 12m at 24.9% margin, the best in the aisle; I assume two rarer pahari lines run below it at 80 and 60 packs at Rs 65/Rs 55 = Rs 8,500. (4) ROASTED CHANA DAL (daliya chana) — assume 80 packs at Rs 70 = Rs 5,600, anchored on whole roasted gram being the biggest SKU in the aisle (Sunil Roasted Gram 200g, 2,384 packs). (5) SAFED MATAR — already listed (09ZH, 27 packs/yr, replenished never); properly stocked assume 120 packs at Rs 44, less the Rs 1,188 already earned = Rs 4,092. (6) SATTU — 1 listed SKU sold 6 packs; a branded facing assume 60 packs at Rs 100 less Rs 588 = Rs 5,412. Sum Rs 46,601. The cooking base behind all of this is ~200-300 resident staff families (students eat in mess; VERIFIED permanent resident base 1,700-2,300 from the 23-day winter-shutdown floor), not 4,700 people — so per-household this is roughly Rs 155-230/yr of extra dal spend, which is why the absolute number is small however real the absence is.
probe_evidence:
Direct SQL sweep over all 21,479 ProductMaster names (VERIFIED, run 2026-08-30): chilka/chhilka/chilca/clika = 0 rows; matki = 0; chowli/chawli/chowla = 0; mangodi/mangori/wadiyan = 0; unpolish% = 0; chholia/cholia/'hara chana' = 0; sprout = 1 (a Nayasa Sprout Maker gadget, 2 sold). So chilka, moth/matki, val/chowli, dal badi/mangodi, unpolished tier, dried green chana and sprouting mixes are GENUINELY ABSENT — the coverage diff was right on these, unlike the toor/almond false positives recorded in Data-Quality-Traps Trap 2.

`ary assort probe unpolished sortex "tata sampann" "24 mantra" "organic tattva"` -> 5 SKUs matched, 5 active, 0 sold, all in Dry Fruits (Tata Sampann Almond/Cashew/Pista/Raisins/Walnuts). No dal. `probe madhi oily oiled` -> 5 matched, all Head & Shoulders shampoo / Cetaphil / one book. `probe chamba kugti bharmour pahari pahadi sirmaur himachali` -> 1 match, "Vegetables Potato Pahari", INACTIVE, 0 sold. `probe bold calibre premium` -> 40 matched across 10 groups, not one chana/chickpea row. `probe "green peas" "hara matar" "safed matar" "white peas" "dry matar" matar` -> 73 matched but every seller is fresh/frozen (Frozen Peas_Z Rs 1,77,975; Peas Fresh Matar_Z Rs 1,31,950; loose Matar Rs 87,666); the only dried row is Raja Dry Matar 500 Gm, 27 packs / Rs 1,188, and "Hara Matar - Rm 1 Gm" is a BOM raw-material row with 0 sales. `probe khichdi khichri` -> 2 matched, both 0 sold (a canteen plate + Nestle Cerelac). `probe roasted chana dal daliya bhuna` -> the Daliya hits are all BROKEN WHEAT (Rajdhani Daliya 1 Kg Rs 1,21,224, Dalia_L Rs 81,400), a different commodity; no roasted split gram. `probe lentil "chickpea pasta" "protein chips" "too yumm"` -> 26 matched, ALL active, ALL zero sold (the entire Too Yumm range). `probe bharat nafed nccf` -> 1 agarbatti. `probe sattu` -> 1 SKU, 6 packs / Rs 588.

THE DECISIVE QUERY (why this is not an assortment problem): of the 146 active core-pulse SKUs, 86 sold nothing in the live 12m window — and joining those 86 to PurchaseDetail/PurchaseHeader (IsDeleted=0), 86 of 86 were NOT PURCHASED ONCE in 12 months, 59 have NEVER been purchased ever, 69 have never been sold ever, and exactly 1 carries any stock (17 units). The dead list includes the exact tiers the demand research says to add: 18 x 250 Gm pulse SKUs (all zero, never bought), 2 x 5 Kg (zero), and the full 6-SKU Amul Organic pulse range (zero). Adding SKU codes to this catalogue provably does nothing — 59 codes prove it.

Second decisive query: Stock.Quantity by warehouse — 46 of the 60 selling core-pulse SKUs carry ZERO or negative on-hand at Ary Pos, the retail counter (41 of 60 are zero/negative across all warehouses). And PurchaseHeader cadence explains every dead month: Raja Kulath Daal bought ONCE in 12m (60 pcs, 2025-12-25) and sold 109 then went dark for 5 months; Raja Mung Daal bought ONCE (2025-09-30) and died after March; Raja Urad Daal bought twice; Raja Arhar Daal bought twice; Raja Lobia 3 POs and 8 zero months. The SKUs with 11-21 POs/yr (Shakti Bhog Besan 21, Raja Chana Black 15, Kabuli Chana 12, Raja Masoor Malka 12) never went dark once.

Margin, derived live from PurchaseDetail.ItemValue/Quantity vs SaleDetail.FinalSaleAmount/Quantity per SKU (NOT the price master, which Trap 4 says is biased high): RETAIL 500g pulses = 14.1% (Rs 52,486 GM on Rs 3,72,223); INSTITUTIONAL Basement = 2.3% (Rs 19,196 GM on Rs 8,40,330), with Mix Dal_L actually NEGATIVE at -0.2%. And the demand research's central economic claim is refuted by ARY's own till: loose Chakki Atta sold by the kg at Ary Pos earns 14.2% (cost Rs 36.00, rate Rs 41.96, 2,362 kg), i.e. the SAME as packaged — this store does not price loose at the 15-30% the research assumes.
top_skus: Urad dal chilka 500 g (Raja or Gtc — line-add on the existing monthly pulse indent; the langar maa-chole di dal input, and ZERO of 21,479 SKUs match chilka in any spelling)

Roasted chana dal / daliya chana 500 g (note: every 'Daliya' SKU ARY sells is BROKEN WHEAT, a different commodity)
Safed matar (dried white peas) 500 g — RESTOCK not add: SKU 09ZH is already listed, sold 27 packs and was never replenished
blockers: THE REAL BLOCKER IS NOT RANGE. 59 of 146 core-pulse SKUs have never been purchased once in their life and 86 of 86 dead SKUs were not bought in the last 12 months. A seventh, eighth or ninth SKU code lands on the same shelf that already ignores 86 of them. Fix replenishment cadence first: the four SKUs that died mid-year (Kulath, Raja Mung Daal, Raja Urad Daal, Raja Lobia) were each ordered once or twice in 12 months, against 11-21 POs/yr for the SKUs that never went dark.

SIZE. The whole honest gap is Rs 46,600/yr of revenue and ~Rs 8,700 of gross margin — 0.06% of the Rs 7.67 Cr store and Rs 725/month of margin. It is not worth a buyer's trip. The Rs 13.3 Cr fleet-wide recommendation total is not reachable through this category.

THE DENOMINATOR TRAP. 69% of 'pulses' (Rs 8,79,331 of Rs 12,75,576) is 14 monthly consignment bills to customer 002CM 'Hunger Heroes', Green Park Main Delhi, booked under ledger group 'Zomato Debtors' — an off-campus wholesale account, at 2.3% gross margin. Any assortment recommendation sized against the category total is 3x too big. Repricing that one account from 2.3% to 6% would add ~Rs 33,000 of gross margin — nearly 4x the entire assortment gap, with zero new SKUs.

THE LOOSE COUNTER THE RESEARCH RECOMMENDS ALREADY EXISTS AND IS NOT RETAIL. All 23 '_L' loose SKUs (Chana White_L, Rajma_L, Kala Chana_L, Mah Dhuli_L, Arhar Dal_L, Besan_L, Moong Sabat_L...) sold on exactly 5 lines each, 100% to Basement, Rs 0 to any resident, in the live window. ARY already runs weighed retail successfully elsewhere (F&V Rs 50.98 L/yr by the kg; loose Chakki Atta 2,362 kg at Ary Pos) so the scale, till and skill exist — but the margin case does not: loose atta earns 14.2%, identical to packed. Opening loose dal to residents is a price-point and channel move, not a margin move, and not an assortment move.

SUPPLIER REACH FROM RAJGARH HP. Chilka, mangodi, roasted chana dal and safed matar are line-adds on the existing Raja/Gtc pulse indent — genuinely easy, days. Bhatt and moth need a Sirmaur/Chamba pahari source that does not exist in the vendor list today; that pair alone is weeks, and it is the highest-margin part of the estimate (~25%), so the margin figure degrades if that sourcing fails.

FOUR OF THE RESEARCH'S LINES ARE ALREADY-FAILED EXPERIMENTS, NOT GAPS — do not re-buy them. Certified organic dal: 6 Amul Organic SKUs listed, zero sold, never purchased. 200-250 g 'baby / convalescent' pack: 18 SKUs listed, all zero, never purchased — and the infant cohort is VERIFIED at 1-2 babies campus-wide (425 diaper packs/yr, 13 formula packs). RTE dal/chole pouches: MTR Dal Makhni and MTR Chana Masala listed, zero. Lentil/pulse protein chips: the whole 26-SKU Too Yumm range listed, zero.

TOOR IS NOT THE #1 DAL HERE. The demand research treats toor/arhar as the must-stock anchor; in this Punjabi/Himachali township retail arhar is 294 packs/yr against kala chana's 1,186 and moong dhuli's 927. Buying toor depth against the national pattern would create dead stock, not sales.

CONFIDENCE LIMIT. Every penetration ratio above (20% chilka share, 100 mangodi packs, 80 bhatt packs) is my judgement anchored on comparable lines on ARY's own shelf, not on any measured demand for the absent item. Nobody has asked a resident. Availability at COMMODITY level is already fine — 12 of 14 pulse commodities sold in all 12 months, only lobia (8 zero months) and kulth (5) had real gaps, together worth ~Rs 11,000/yr — so the aisle is small because ~200-300 cooking households is a small base, not because the shelf is broken.
kill_reason: Not a kill, but a strong downgrade, and the evidence is worth stating as one. The 19 lines the coverage diff called "missing" ARE genuinely missing — I re-probed every one with multiple spellings and a direct sweep over all 21,479 catalogue names, and chilka, matki, chowli, mangodi, unpolished, chholia and sprouting mixes return literally zero rows. So this is not a Trap-2 name-match artefact. But they are worth Rs 46,600 of revenue and Rs 8,700 of gross margin a year in total, because the retail aisle they would sit in is only Rs 3,96,245/yr and the cooking base is ~200-300 staff households, not 4,700 residents. Meanwhile the constraint that actually binds is stocking, not range: 86 of the 146 active core-pulse SKUs sold nothing in the live 12 months, and NOT ONE of those 86 was purchased even once in that window — 59 of them have never been purchased in their entire life and 69 have never been sold. 46 of the 60 SKUs that DO sell carry zero or negative on-hand at Ary Pos right now. The four SKUs that died mid-year each had one or two purchase orders in 12 months against 11-21 for the SKUs that never went dark. And the catalogue already contains, unbought, the precise tiers the demand research recommends adding — 18 x 250 g packs, 2 x 5 kg, and the whole 6-SKU Amul Organic range. That is the proof that a recommendation to ADD is the wrong instrument here: this store does not have a range problem, it has a replenishment problem and a channel problem (69% of the category is a 2.3%-margin Delhi wholesale pass-through, and every loose SKU is withheld from residents). Add the six lines if a buyer is calling the supplier anyway — they cost nothing to append to an existing indent — but do not carry a pulses number into the fleet total as an assortment opportunity.
